items.title: What Moksy is and the customer journey
items.body: Moksy turns an idea into a build-ready plan. You type in your idea and an AI asks a series of questions in what the product calls the interview. Your answers become the input to a document: the plan for your idea. After the document comes an expert review, where a reviewer checks it, and then the build stage, which covers downloads, exports and hiring. One idea and its document live inside a project. Customers create projects and receive documents; reviewers check documents; staff run the platform from an operator console. A person's role decides what they can do. In the customer area the home screen is called Home.

items.title: MOX and MXP
items.body: Moksy has two coined marks that are one letter apart. MOX stands for Moksy credit, and 1 MOX equals one cent. MXP stands for Moksy Experience Points, and it is what you climb the Ladder with. Always pair the unit with a noun so they cannot be confused: the Wallet holds MOX, the Ladder is climbed with MXP. MOX lives in the Wallet, can be bought in packs, is granted as Starter MOX on joining, and is held in escrow while a review is open.

items.title: Where the numbers in your document come from
items.body: The report is the centre of the product, and the rule is that every number, name, date and judgement shown to a customer should resolve to a stored fact with a source. A model may phrase a figure but may never originate one. If a fact is missing, the system refuses, asks, derives or gives a band rather than inventing a number. Your interview answers are the input to your document.
